title: Technology Sector Update for 04/30/2018: TWTR,BIDU,CYRN,MSFT,JASO

Technology stocks fell Monday afternoon, giving back their earlier gains, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing almost 0.5% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 0.9% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Twitter ( TWTR ) rose Monday, climbing as much as 6%, after the micro-blogging website said it has will create live content and advertising opportunities for the Walt Disney Co. ( DIS ) from across the entire Disney portfolio on the Twitter platform. The new deal includes Twitter and Disney's ESPN sports network working together to produce specific live shows in development this week at their NewFront presentations later today and on Wednesday. Separately, Twitter confirmed it sold data access to the same Cambridge academic who obtained Facebook ( FB ) user data. Twitter confirmed to The (UK) Telegraph on Saturday that Global Science Research and Alexksarder Kogan purchased one-time access to a random sample of public tweets from a five-month period between December 2014 and April 2015. But the company also told Bloomberg it did not provide access to private data on Twitter users.
In other sector news:
- Cyren ( CYRN ) has turned fractionally lower lower, giving back a more than 4% advance earlier in the session after announcing a collaboration with Microsoft ( MSFT ) to improve the detection of phishing attacks and advanced malware in Microsoft Office 365. Cyren said its Threat Intelligence Services and GlobalView security intelligence cloud will be integrated in the Office 365 network and result in material contract expansion valued at $20 million for the cyber-security firm over the next three years.
- Baidu ( BIDU ) was trading lower on Monday, falling over 2%, after the Chinese internet and e-commerce company said it has agreed to sell a majority stake in its financial services unit to a consortium of investors led by TPG Capital and Carlyle Group for $1.9 billion. The deal will leave Baidu with 42% of the wealth management and consumer lending subsidiary, which will be renamed Du Xiaoman Financial.
- JA Solar (JASO) declined Monday after reporting fiscal Q4 net income trailing year-ago comparisons despite a 42% year-over-year jump in revenue. Excluding one-time items, the photovoltaic-panels company earned RMB2.46 per American depository share, or about $0.38 per ADS, down from RMB6.80 per share during the same quarter last year but still topping the two-analyst consensus expecting $0.12 per ADS. Revenue during the three months ended Dec. 31 rose to RMB5.67 billion, or about $871.8 million, from RMB3.99 billion during the year-ago period, also exceeding the $633.7 million analyst mean.
